portfolio.codebook_interaction: The first term applies equal-and-opposite tangential forces to the two assigned codewords, increasing the component of their separation aligned with the directed item displacement. Because the force is projected orthogonally to their current separation, its instantaneous first-order change in squared pair distance is zero; it does not pull the pair together. The usage penalty spreads soft source-assignment mass across codes. Assignment indices are detached, while distances and codeword vectors remain differentiable.
portfolio.falsifier: Reject if the checker finds a non-finite or zero codebook gradient, if exchanging source and target leaves the loss unchanged, if the measured transition-pair codeword separation decreases, or if the cold run fails to raise Stage-3 recall@10 while keeping level-0 Gini no higher than control, L1-to-L2 branches per code no lower than control, train-to-test frequency drift no higher than control, and sequence information no lower than control.
portfolio.risk: The tangential update may rotate codeword boundaries without improving the positive-pair match rate, or may alter higher-level residual assignments and prefix structure despite the level-0 usage penalty. The usage penalty can also be too weak to prevent concentration or too strong to impair useful specialization. The single frozen evaluation could therefore show no recall gain even if pair geometry changes.

portfolio.codebook_interaction: Gradients flow through both soft assignment distributions into the codebook, moving Voronoi geometry to preserve informative ordered transitions and balanced source usage. The joint-information term rewards predictable but non-independent source and target codes; it does not contain a same-code attraction or a pairwise codeword-distance minimization, so it has no direct force pulling the two codewords together. Soft assignments avoid nondifferentiable hard-index gradients.
portfolio.falsifier: Reject if swapping source and target does not change the loss on a nondegenerate checker batch, if any declared gradient is zero or non-finite, or if the cold run does not improve Stage-3 recall@10 while meeting the control-relative Gini, prefix-branch, train-to-test drift, and sequence-information requirements.
portfolio.risk: The objective can increase mutual information by encoding batch-specific or unstable transition patterns rather than useful held-out sequence structure. Its soft joint estimates may also be noisy at the available batch size, and the balance penalty on source marginals does not guarantee that the full three-level prefix tree or train-to-test frequency drift is preserved.

portfolio.codebook_interaction: The normalized transport term moves each assigned codeword so their directed displacement tracks the behavior-conditioned residual displacement. The separation barrier has gradient only when the assigned pair is closer than m and pushes the two codewords apart; it never pulls them together. Nearest-code indices are detached, but residual vectors and codeword vectors remain differentiable. If the barrier is inactive, transport can still alter pair distance, so the barrier margin must be calibrated above the observed collapse regime.
portfolio.falsifier: Reject if the checker finds a zero or non-finite declared gradient, if exchanging source and target leaves the loss unchanged, or if the cold run shows reduced pair separation, increased level-0 Gini, fewer L1-to-L2 branches per code, increased train-to-test frequency drift, reduced sequence information, or no Stage-3 recall@10 improvement over control.
portfolio.risk: Residual transport may overfit training transitions, disrupt higher-level residual quantization, or satisfy the minimum-separation barrier by spreading codewords in directions that do not preserve useful prefix branches. The barrier prevents close-pair collapse but does not itself guarantee balanced level-0 usage, sequence information, or downstream retrieval quality.
